sun.upright:
An old man standing still on a mountain with a lamp is about the last thing an Aries Sun expects to be handed. You're cardinal fire, ruled by Mars, and you find out who you are by doing, by going first, by taking on the fight nobody else wants. The Hermit belongs to Virgo, and Virgo and Aries sit five signs apart in a quincunx, which in plain terms means they share nothing and only get on through a lot of small adjustments. Fire and earth aren't enemies. They've just never been introduced, and you're the one who has to do it.

What the card wants from your Sun is a stretch of thinking before the next move, and I'd guess that's already irritating you a bit. Aries Suns are proud of being decisive, and fair enough, since your first instinct is usually right. The Hermit has no quarrel with that. It's pointing at a question underneath, about what you actually want to be building, and you won't hear the answer over the noise of your own momentum. The Emperor is Aries's Major, a man on a throne running things. The Hermit is closer to what he'd look like if he walked out of the palace for a month to work out whether he still wanted the job. Most Aries Suns come back from a month like that clearer and just as fierce.

At work it can show as an offer or a new venture you'd normally say yes to on the spot. In sport or training it might be a season spent on technique instead of speed. Before you start the next big thing, spend three days telling nobody about it.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, the Hermit can leave an Aries Sun refusing to stop at all. Every pause feels like losing ground, so you push the launch, send the email, take the job, and work out afterwards whether you wanted any of it. Mars rules Aries and hates waiting, and with the card reversed there's nobody in you asking the slower question.

The other version is rarer and harder to spot. Something knocked your confidence, a knock-back at work or a plan that fell over in public, and you've gone quiet and called it reflection when it's closer to sulking. It shows in a project you've stopped mentioning, and in a friend you haven't rung because ringing would feel like admitting the loss. Pick the small, dull task you've been avoiding since then, and get it done before you decide anything bigger.

moon.upright:
Feelings in an Aries Moon come in hot and leave fast. You're annoyed and you know it straight away, you say so, and an hour later you've half forgotten why. What settles you is movement, a hard walk, a workout, a job you can throw yourself at. The Hermit settles by staying still, and that's the whole difficulty with this pairing. Virgo and Aries are a quincunx apart, five signs, no shared element and no shared mode, and fire and earth have very little to say to each other until someone makes them talk.

So the card is asking your Moon to sit with a feeling for longer than feels natural. For you that can be physically uncomfortable. The body wants to do something with the heat, and here you're being asked to leave it where it is and find out what it's actually about. I've seen Aries Moons discover, doing this, that half their anger was tiredness and the other half was hurt, and that neither needed shouting at anyone. Mars rules Aries, and a Mars Moon keeps the body braced for trouble. The Hermit is offering a kind of rest where nothing's being fought.

Sleep is where it shows first, since an Aries Moon tends to go to bed wired and wake too early. It shows with family, where you flare and forgive inside an hour and still wish you hadn't flared. Next time you feel the heat come up, go and sit somewhere on your own for ten minutes before you say anything, and leave the phone where it is.
moon.reversed:
When the Hermit turns over on an Aries Moon, you can end up filling every quiet minute so there's no room to feel anything. Gym, work, a night out, another project. It looks like energy, and underneath it there's usually one feeling you'd prefer not to meet on your own.

Or the fire goes out and you brood. You go over an argument in bed, win it several times, and wake up angrier than you went to sleep, while the card's Virgo streak picks at how badly you handled it. That tends to show in sleep, in a short fuse with people who've done nothing, and with a partner who's getting the edge of a mood that isn't about them. Get the feeling moving through the body first, a run or a hard clean of the kitchen, and then tell one person plainly how you are.

rising.upright:
Aries rising comes through the door first. Mars rules your chart, and strangers tend to read you as quick, direct, a bit of a challenge, the one who'll ask the blunt question in the first five minutes. The Hermit has about the slowest entrance in the deck. He barely enters at all. He stands off to one side with his lamp and watches. Virgo sits five signs from Aries, a quincunx, so nothing about this fits naturally, and the card and your Ascendant have to keep adjusting to each other.

What it does is put a pause at the front of how you meet things. You may notice you're holding back in rooms where you'd usually take over, watching who talks to whom before you pick a side. For Aries rising that can feel out of character, even a bit flat. The people around you are likely to read it differently. They see someone who's listening, which with your chart ruler is rare enough to get noticed. The instinct hasn't gone anywhere, and you'll still move fast when it counts. You're just choosing the moment, and first impressions tend to go better for it.

It helps in a new job, where the first fortnight is better spent learning who actually decides things. On first dates it makes you easier company and less of a contest. In any meeting where you'd normally speak first, let two other people go ahead of you, and listen for what they give away.
rising.reversed:
Reversed on Aries rising, the Hermit either gets shoved aside or takes over completely. The first version is you barging in harder than usual, deciding what a room's about before you've heard anyone, so people brace a little when they see you coming. Mars rules your chart, and when you're rattled it pushes.

The second version is odder on you. An Aries Ascendant is normally open and forward, so when you go guarded and watchful it usually means something stung, a rejection or a public mistake, and you've pulled the shutters down at the front. It shows in shorter replies, in parties you leave early, and in a new workplace where people have quietly decided you're aloof. Go first with something small and friendly, a question about the other person, and let your usual directness come back that way.

sun.upright:
Of all the signs, Taurus is one of the least bothered by the Hermit. Fixed earth, ruled by Venus, you already know how to wait, how to build slowly, how to enjoy your own company on a Sunday with nothing planned. The card belongs to Virgo, the next earth sign along, and the two sit in a trine, four signs apart, the easiest angle there is. Same element too, so the card speaks your language and makes whatever's already in you louder, the patience and the digging in alike.

The patience is the gift. You aren't waiting for anyone's permission to be who you are, and the Hermit gives that patience a sharper eye, so you can tell which of the long slow things are worth the years. Virgo is fussier than Taurus about quality, and a bit of that fussiness suits you. The digging in is the catch. The Hierophant is Taurus's Major, a card of tradition and doing things the way they've always been done, and put that beside a card about solitude and you can end up very comfortable, very sure of yourself, and quite hard to reach. I've seen Taurus Suns go a whole year like that without noticing the friends dropping off.

At work it's a good card for a skill you've been building for years, a trade, a craft, something people will pay properly for. With money it favours slow, careful choices, and you're unlikely to be tempted by anything flashy. Ring the friend you've been meaning to see for about three months, and put a date in the diary.
sun.reversed:
With the Hermit upside down, a Taurus Sun can dig in and call it knowing its own mind. You've decided, you won't revisit it, and the time alone that was meant for thinking has turned into time spent defending a position nobody's attacking. Fixed earth is hard to shift at the best of times, and with two earth signs in play there's nothing loose in the mix.

It shows in money, where caution has become never spending on the thing that would make life better, and in the body, which stiffens when a routine has no give in it. It shows in a grudge that's outlasted its reason. Venus rules Taurus and does best when there's some pleasure in the day. Change one small part of your routine, keep the change for a month, and notice who comments on it.

moon.upright:
A Taurus Moon settles through the body. Good food, a warm bed, the same walk at the same time, someone's hand on your back. You feel safe when nothing's lurching, and you can go a long way on very simple comforts. The Hermit is gentle with all that. Its sign, Virgo, is earth like your Moon and sits in a trine to Taurus, four signs along, so the card and your feelings want much the same things, quiet, slowness and being left alone for a bit.

Mostly, then, the card is agreeing with you. A quiet stretch may be doing you real good, a few weekends in, a phone that stays face down, evenings where nobody needs anything from you. Venus rules Taurus, and a Venus Moon enjoys its own space when it's a nice space. What the Hermit adds is a Virgo question about which comforts are actually helping. The third biscuit isn't doing the same job as the first. Two earth signs together can overdo it, and a Taurus Moon slides from resting into hiding without any clear line between them. Usually the tell is whether you come out of a quiet weekend more open to people or a bit more shut.

Sleep is one place it shows, and it's likely to be deep and long. Food's another, especially what you reach for when you're low. With a partner it can mean needing more time on your own than they're used to, which is worth explaining before it gets misread. Cook one proper meal for yourself and eat it at the table with no screen.
moon.reversed:
Comfort can become a place to hide when the Hermit turns over on a Taurus Moon. Same sofa, same food, same three people, and it gets called self-care when mostly it's a way of not being unsettled by anything. The Virgo edge of the card doesn't help, because it gets turned on you, and a quiet voice keeps saying you've let yourself go.

The body tends to carry it first, a heaviness, poor sleep, eating that's stopped being a pleasure. At home it can look like a room you've made so safe you don't want to leave it, and a slow loneliness you haven't said out loud because saying it would mean changing something. Venus rules Taurus and needs a bit of pleasure from outside the house as well. Say yes to the next invitation you'd normally turn down, and stay at least an hour.

rising.upright:
Taurus rising doesn't hurry into a room, and people tend to relax when you arrive. Venus rules your chart, so there's a pleasant, solid ease to how you come across, and strangers often decide you're reliable before you've said much. The Hermit belongs to Virgo, another earth sign, four signs away in a trine, and it lays its quiet watchfulness straight over that. There's nothing to translate. You're likely coming across as calm, private and a bit hard to read, in a way most people find reassuring.

Your instinct at the start of anything is to take your time, and the card backs you. You might be watching more than talking at first meetings, working out who's who before you commit to anyone, and that's a sound instinct for a Taurus Ascendant. The Hierophant is Taurus's own Major, the teacher on the throne, and with the Hermit on top people may treat you as someone who knows things, the one to ask. The catch with the same element doubled is that calm can look closed. Quick or nervous people especially can leave a first meeting not knowing whether you liked them, and to be honest you might not have decided yet.

It shows in the early weeks of a new job, where your slowness to open up can read as caution or as coolness depending on who's looking. On first dates the steadiness is attractive as long as some warmth comes with it. Ask the next new person you meet one real question about themselves, and let them see you enjoy the answer.
rising.reversed:
Upside down on Taurus rising, the Hermit's reserve can set hard. The calm that usually reassures people starts to look like a closed door, and you come across as someone who's already made up their mind about everyone. Some of that is plain stubbornness, which Taurus and this card share. Some of it is nerves, because a fixed earth Ascendant copes with a new room by not moving much.

It shows in new situations you avoid because the routine is easier, and in first impressions that stay stuck, yours of other people and theirs of you. A bad start with a colleague can go uncorrected for months. Venus rules your chart and is at its best when it's warm. Next time you meet someone, let them surprise you before you decide who they are, and tell them one thing about yourself they didn't ask for.

sun.upright:
Mercury rules both Gemini and Virgo, so this card is no stranger to your Sun. It's the other thing your own planet does. In Gemini, Mercury collects, talks, links one idea to the next and moves on. In Virgo it sits down with what it's collected and works out which bits are true. The two signs are square, three apart and both mutable, which is the angle that grates until you do something about it. Earth and air are opposed as well, so the friction is between the clever idea and whether it actually works.

You build yourself out of ideas, and you're proud of being quick. The Hermit wants to know whether any of it holds up once you're alone with it and there's nobody to bounce it off. That can feel deflating. Gemini Suns often do their best thinking out loud, and being told to go quiet can sound like being told to think less. It's closer to being asked to finish a thought for once. The Lovers is Gemini's Major, and it's a card about choosing, and the Hermit more or less makes the choice for you, one idea taken all the way down, with the others put away for a while.

At work it shows as the report or the course or the side project that's been ninety percent done for far too long. With money it's the fine print you usually skim. Close most of your open browser tabs, pick the one project that matters, and give it two evenings on its own.
sun.reversed:
Reversed, the Hermit leaves a Gemini Sun spinning. You read, forward, comment, start, and none of it lands, and the part of Mercury that checks and finishes things never gets a turn. People start to think of you as clever and hard to rely on, and you can feel them thinking it.

Or the square jams the other way and you go uncharacteristically silent, stuck on one worry, running the same three sentences round your head with nothing new let in. That shows in sleep, with a mind that won't switch off at midnight, and at work, in projects that quietly expire. It can show with a sibling or an old friend you've been meaning to call back for weeks. Take one open loop, an unpaid invoice, an unanswered email, a half-read contract, and close it completely before you open anything new.

moon.upright:
A Gemini Moon works out what it feels by talking. You text three people, send a voice note, read up on whatever's bothering you until it makes sense, and usually by then you feel better. The Hermit would like you to try it the other way round, a bit of quiet with the feeling before you put words on it. Virgo squares Gemini from three signs away, and earth and air are opposed, so there's real friction here between a mind that wants to explain and a body that just wants to feel.

The odd thing is that you and the card share a ruler. Mercury looks after both signs, so this isn't a foreign language. It's your own mind being asked to use its slower gear. Gemini Moons tend to live from the neck up, and when things get hard the talking speeds up to keep pace, which only makes the worry louder. What the Hermit offers is a break from your own commentary. Some feelings don't want explaining. Give them ten minutes of silence and they're often half the size.

It shows in sleep, when the phone's in bed with you and your head won't close the tabs. It shows in friendships, where one or two people have become your regular sounding board and might be wearing a bit thin. With a sibling it can be a conversation that goes better if you let them do the talking. When the next worry comes, keep it to yourself for a full day before you tell anyone, and notice what it's turned into by then.
moon.reversed:
With the Hermit reversed, a Gemini Moon can keep so many conversations going that nothing's ever felt all the way through. It looks sociable, and some of it is avoidance. There's usually one quiet feeling under the busy inbox, and you're not letting it have the floor.

The other version is the anxious loop, Mercury going round and round one worry with no fresh air, picking at it until it's twice the size it started. It shows in broken sleep and a jittery body you can't talk your way out of, and in friends who've started to feel like an audience. Get it out of your head and into your hands, a walk, cooking, weeding, anything with no words in it. Then take one real feeling to one person, the whole of it.

rising.upright:
Gemini rising arrives mid-sentence. Mercury rules your chart, and people meeting you usually see someone quick, funny and curious, with three questions asked before anyone's sat down. The Hermit is the quietest figure in the deck, off by himself with a lamp. You share a ruler, since Mercury looks after Virgo too, but Virgo squares Gemini, and air and earth pull in opposite directions, so this is a scratchy fit.

What it does to your first impression is slow it down. You might notice you're saying less at the start of things and watching more, and it can feel strange, as if the charm's been turned down. People tend to take it well. Gemini rising is great company and can also leave a stranger unsure whether you actually took them in, and with the Hermit over you they're likely to feel you did. Your wit still works. It lands harder after a pause, and people start leaning in when you speak where they'd normally just wait for the next joke.

It shows in interviews, where one careful answer will do more for you than five quick ones. It shows on first dates, where listening properly is rarer than you'd think and people remember it, and with a new neighbour or colleague. At the next event where you'd normally work the room, stay with one person for twenty minutes and ask about something they care about.
rising.reversed:
When Gemini rising refuses the reversed Hermit, the mask goes all surface. You talk faster to fill the gaps, joke the moment anything turns real, and walk away from a first meeting having given nothing of yourself. People start to find you slippery, and they're not always wrong.

Or it swings hard the other way. The breezy front goes stiff and careful, every sentence edited before it's out, Mercury fretting about how you're coming across until you hardly come across at all. That shows in interviews, where you might be word-perfect and forgettable, in new friendships that never quite get going, and on dates, where the patter keeps anyone from getting close. Say one plain, true thing about yourself early in the next conversation, with no clever angle on it, and leave a gap afterwards.

sun.upright:
The Hermit and a Cancer Sun get on better than you'd expect. Cardinal water, ruled by the Moon, you build yourself around the people you look after and the home you make for them, and you're proud of that, even when you don't say so. The Hermit's sign, Virgo, sits two along from Cancer in a sextile, a friendly angle, and earth and water are natural allies in astrology, the earth giving water somewhere to go and the water keeping the earth alive. So the card isn't fighting you. It's lending you something.

What it lends is a bit of distance from everyone you care for. Cancer Suns can end up so needed that they don't really know what they'd do with an afternoon to themselves, and some of that is pride, being the one everyone relies on. The Hermit wants you to have a part of your life that's yours alone. The Chariot is Cancer's Major, the driver in armour pushing forward, and the Hermit is close to the opposite picture, one man on foot, going slowly, on his own. You need both, and you've probably had a lot more of the first lately. A sextile is an opening that still has to be taken, so none of this happens unless you make the room for it.

At home it can show as a spare room, a shed, or a Saturday morning that belongs to nobody else. With family it might mean stepping back from organising every gathering. Tell the people you live with that one evening a week is yours, and keep to it.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, the Hermit can send a Cancer Sun into its shell to nurse a wound, and the solitude that was meant to restore you turns into somewhere to go over who let you down. You're still caring for everyone. You're also quietly keeping score, and the resentment builds in exactly the place a boundary should have gone.

With water and earth this friendly, things can pool and go still. A mood hangs around for days. Home becomes a place to hide. Being needed starts to feel safer than being seen. It shows in sleep, in comfort eating, and in a friend you've gone cold on without ever telling them why. Say the thing you've been swallowing to the person it belongs to, and then let somebody look after you for an evening.

moon.upright:
A Cancer Moon remembers everything. The tone of a voice on the phone five years ago, a birthday that got forgotten, the smell of a grandmother's kitchen. The Moon rules Cancer, so this is the Moon in its own sign, feeling at full volume and needing somewhere safe to put it. Virgo makes an easy sextile to Cancer, and the elements, earth and water, have always got on, so the card comes in kindly. What it offers is a stretch of quiet where the feelings can come and go with nobody else there to manage.

That's more useful to you than it sounds, because a Cancer Moon picks up other people's moods constantly and loses track of its own. You walk into a room, someone's upset, and within minutes you're upset too and can't quite say whose it was. Time on your own sorts that out. The lamp the Hermit holds is a small light, enough to see a few steps, and that's about the right scale for this. You don't have to understand everything you feel. It's enough to notice which feelings came home with you from somebody else.

At home it shows as a need for a room or a corner where the door can shut. In the body it's sleep, which tends to deepen once you feel safe, and food, which a Cancer Moon leans on for comfort more than it lets on. With family it can mean stepping back from someone else's crisis long enough to rest. Run a bath, lock the door, and leave the phone in another room.
moon.reversed:
For a Cancer Moon, the upside-down Hermit's quiet can turn into a cave. You shut the shell and stay in there, taking old hurts out one at a time and turning them over. The Virgo side of the card adds a critical edge, so on top of the hurt you're telling yourself off for having it.

Earth and water left too still go muddy. Moods settle in and won't shift, the past gets more attention than the present, and home becomes a place to get away from everyone. It shows in disturbed sleep and eating for comfort, and in holding people off while wishing they'd come closer. The Moon rules Cancer, and its feelings are meant to come and go. Ring the person you miss, and let the call be a bit awkward if it has to be.

rising.upright:
Cancer rising comes into a room sideways. You feel it out first, work out who's safe, and only then say much, and strangers tend to read you as kind and a little shy, with every mood showing on your face. The Moon rules your chart, so that face changes a lot. The Hermit sits comfortably over it. Virgo makes a sextile to Cancer, an easy angle, and earth and water get on, so from the outside the card's watchfulness and your caution look like the same thing.

People may be meeting a quieter, more self-contained version of you than usual, and that can work well. A Cancer Ascendant usually offers care before it offers an opinion, and with the Hermit on top there's a sense that you're paying close attention, which makes people feel safe quickly. The risk is that the shell looks thicker. Some people will read the reserve as coolness and won't try again, and Cancer rising takes that personally, even when the reserve was what put them off. The Chariot is Cancer's own Major, the driver behind armour, and this card pulls a hood up over the armour. That's fine as long as people can see you smile under it.

It shows in a new job, where you'll probably be the one who notices who's struggling, and in meeting a partner's friends, where you may hang back longer than you mean to. Remember one small thing someone tells you at a first meeting, and bring it up the next time you see them.
rising.reversed:
With the Hermit reversed, Cancer rising can go defensive at the door. The shell snaps shut at the first hint of threat, and people meet a guardedness they can't get past, sometimes a moodiness that has them treading carefully. You read danger into a stranger who was only being a stranger.

The card's reserve on top of yours means you can pull back at the exact moment someone reaches out, and then feel hurt that nobody tried harder. It shows in parties you leave early, in first impressions that come across as cold, and in a new workplace where a throwaway comment gets taken to heart. The Moon rules your chart, so the mood leaks out whatever you do. Assume goodwill for the first five minutes of the next meeting, and ask the other person how their day's been.

sun.upright:
Leo Suns want to be seen doing the thing. Fixed fire, ruled by the Sun, you're at your best in front of people, warming a room, taking the credit you've earned, and there's nothing wrong with that. The Hermit works in the dark, on a mountain, with one small lamp, and he never takes a bow. Virgo is the sign right after Leo, and neighbouring signs have very little in common, which is exactly why each tends to have what the other's missing. Fire and earth are neutral as well, no pull either way, so this takes some effort from you.

What the card is lending your Sun is a taste for the part of the work nobody claps for. You probably know the feeling of having the big idea and all the confidence and then getting bored in the middle, when it's admin and practice and nobody's watching. That middle is where the Hermit lives. Strength is Leo's own Major, and it's about a kind of power that stays calm and doesn't need to be looked at, so this is less foreign to you than it seems. The pride you get from doing something properly in private is steadier, and it doesn't drain away the minute the audience goes home. I've seen Leo Suns find this in their late twenties and get very good at something as a result.

At work it shows as the skill you need to master before the next stage, the rehearsal before the performance. With money it can mean handling things quietly and well where you'd usually spend to impress. Pick one thing you normally do for show and do it once for nobody, just to get it right.
sun.reversed:
The reversed Hermit can leave a Leo Sun unable to bear an empty room. If nobody's going to see it, it doesn't feel worth doing, so the careful, private part of the work gets skipped, and you keep performing when what was needed was a quiet week of getting it right.

Or it goes the other way and you retreat in a huff. The applause didn't come, someone else got the credit, and you've gone off to your cave and called it dignity. That shows at work after a promotion goes elsewhere, in a friendship you've let cool because you felt overlooked, and in a body worn down from putting on a show while running on empty. The Sun rules Leo and needs warmth coming back to it. Do one generous thing nobody will ever find out about, and pay attention to how it feels afterwards.

moon.upright:
There's a particular kind of tired a Leo Moon gets after a big night, a party you hosted, a week where you were everyone's favourite. You were lit up the whole time, and afterwards you feel oddly flat. The Sun rules Leo, and a Sun-ruled Moon feels safest when it's warmed by other people's attention. The Hermit, drawn for your tides, offers a very different warmth, the sort you get from being on your own and finding you're fine. Virgo sits right next to Leo, neighbours with little in common, and fire and earth have to be introduced, so at first this can feel like being sent to your room.

Stay with it and something shifts. A Leo Moon's sense of being alright can ride on the last thing someone said, a compliment, a like, a friend who didn't reply. That's an exhausting way to live, and you probably know it. The Hermit gives your feelings a floor that doesn't move depending on who's watching. It's quieter than you're used to. It also means the next time someone forgets your birthday, it stings and then passes, and the week survives. Strength is Leo's Major, and the calm in that card is already in you somewhere, under the need to be seen.

It shows after social highs, in the dip that follows, when you'd normally go looking for more attention. It shows in family, where you're the warm one and can end up feeling unseen, and in sleep, which suffers when approval runs low. Keep one small habit that's only for you, a walk, a sketchbook, a swim, and don't tell anyone about it.
moon.reversed:
When the Hermit's reversed, a Leo Moon can go hungry for attention and let it show. If the messages slow down you feel it in your chest, you fish a bit, and a quiet evening lands like a snub. The solitude on offer feels like being left, so you fill it with noise and come away hungrier.

The rarer version is proud and silent. You're hurt, you won't say so, and you refuse the comfort you actually want because asking would dent your pride. The Virgo side of the card turns critical and tells you you're too much, or not enough. It shows in big swings of mood, in poor sleep after a slight, and in friends kept at a careful distance since one felt let-down. Let one person see you tired and unimpressive, and let them stay for dinner anyway.

rising.upright:
Leo rising makes an entrance whether it means to or not. The Sun rules your chart, and people notice the warmth first, the laugh, the hair, the sense that you've arrived and the room's a bit brighter for it. The Hermit over that doorway is the neighbour who stayed in. Virgo is the next sign along from Leo, and adjacent signs have little in common, so the card lends your front something it doesn't naturally have, a modest, watchful reserve. Fire and earth have no built-in bond, so it takes a bit of practice to wear.

People may notice you're a notch quieter going in. That can bother a Leo Ascendant, because there's a worry that turning down means disappearing. It doesn't. The warmth still comes off you. What changes is that people feel you're actually looking at them, and they relax. I've seen Leo rising do this and find people coming over to them at parties where usually they'd be doing the circuit. Strength, Leo's own Major, is about a presence that doesn't have to push, and the Hermit brings some of that to your first impression.

It shows in first meetings of every kind, a new team, a friend's wedding, a first date. At work it shows in pitches, where a pause before your big line makes people listen harder. Walk into the next room without trying to warm it up, and put all your attention on whoever you end up talking to.
rising.reversed:
Upside down on Leo rising, the Hermit gets ignored and the display takes over. You're unsure, so you perform harder, more story, more warmth, more you, and people leave a bit worn out and not certain who they met. Some quiet at the door would have let a few of them come to you.

The other tilt is the proud retreat. After a knock, the sunny front goes cool and you stand at the edge of the room daring anyone to notice. The Virgo eye picks at how you're landing until you second-guess the whole entrance. It shows at parties you either run or avoid, at work when a new boss hasn't warmed to you yet, and in first impressions that come across as too much or oddly aloof. Go into the next room at half volume, and let your interest in other people do what the performance usually does.

sun.upright:
This is your own card. The Hermit is Virgo's Major, so a Virgo Sun drawing it is the sign meeting its own portrait, and there's no translating to do. Mutable earth, ruled by Mercury, you build yourself through being good at things, through careful work, through noticing what everyone else missed. The man on the mountain with his lamp is doing much the same, finding the one true thing and holding it up so others can see. Being the same element, the card turns everything up, the gifts and the faults together.

At its best this is you at full strength. You know your subject, you trust your eye, and you don't need anyone in the room to tell you the work is good. Virgo Suns often have a quiet authority they don't quite claim, and the Hermit asks you to claim it, to be the person others come to for the proper answer. The trouble with a card that agrees with you completely is that it agrees with your worst habit too. The eye that improves things can turn on you, and then nothing's ever finished and nothing's ever good enough, least of all you. I've seen a lot of Virgo Suns lose years to a project they wouldn't let go of because it wasn't perfect yet.

At work it shows as polishing past the point where anyone can tell the difference. In health it can be a body either fussed over or ignored, and with people it's the safe distance of the one who observes. Call one thing done that's merely good, and hand it over before you look at it again.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, your own card shows you the Virgo shadow at full size. The eye for detail becomes a machine for finding faults, first in the work, then in other people, then in you, and it never runs out of material. Time alone stops being useful and starts to sour.

With earth on earth there's nothing to lighten it, so it can spiral. Decisions stall under analysis. Worry passes itself off as being thorough. The self-criticism gets so constant you barely hear it any more. It shows in projects that never go out, in a body watched for symptoms, and in warmth held back from people because they've fallen short too. Mercury rules Virgo and will always find one more thing. Forgive one small mistake of your own out loud, to someone, and leave it there.

moon.upright:
A Virgo Moon calms down by putting things in order. The drawer sorted, the bench wiped, the list ticked, a problem you can quietly fix for someone. Mercury rules Virgo, and your feelings often come out as tasks, which is why you clean when you're upset. The Hermit is Virgo's own card, so drawing it for your tides is your emotional nature meeting itself, earth on earth, and the pull to go off alone and sift a feeling down to what's actually true comes twice as strong.

That's soothing, mostly. You probably know how much a quiet, tidy evening resets you, and how frayed you get after a chaotic week with no time to yourself. The catch with the doubled sign is that the quiet can turn into a courtroom. You sit alone, go through the day, and find yourself guilty of being too much, or too little, or too messy about a feeling that was perfectly reasonable. Solitude only rests a Virgo Moon when it stays kind. You'll know which sort you've been having by how you feel the next morning.

In the body it shows as sleep that improves on a settled routine and suffers when the list's too long. At home it's the order that keeps you calm, and the edge in your voice when someone disturbs it. In a relationship it can mean helping so busily that nobody thinks to ask how you are. Let one feeling be felt without trying to solve it, and go to bed with the dishes in the sink.
moon.reversed:
With your own card reversed, a Virgo Moon can turn all that fixing on itself and not stop. The routine that usually soothes hardens into rules you punish yourself for breaking, and the quiet you need becomes a place to list everything wrong with you. Rest never quite arrives, because there's always one more thing to sort first.

Doubled earth gives the worry nowhere to go, so it pools. Anxious tidying. A body checked for faults. Feelings managed where they should be felt. It shows in sleep broken by tomorrow's list, in comfort that only comes once everything's under control, and in a harshness you save mostly for yourself. Leave one thing undone on purpose and notice that nothing falls down. Then let someone look after you without making them earn it.

rising.upright:
Virgo rising meets the world the way this card does, quietly, taking a careful reading before stepping in. Mercury rules your chart, and strangers usually notice the neatness, the good questions, the sense that you've done your homework. The Hermit is Virgo's own Major, so on your Ascendant it's hardly a mask at all. It's your usual face, doubled. People meet someone modest and observant who says less than they notice, and they tend to trust you for it, since you're plainly not selling anything.

That's a real strength. You read a room accurately, you rarely overreach at the door, and people sense that your quiet means you're paying proper attention. The doubling has a downside, though. Modest can slide into invisible, and observant can slide into judging from the sidelines, and with the card on top you might hang back so far that warmer people never find out you were interested. Some of what you've been left out of lately, and you'll know which, happened because nobody could tell you wanted in. Watching from the edge is comfortable, and it costs you.

It shows in new jobs, where you'll be seen as capable and possibly as a bit cool. It shows at parties, in the quiet critique running in your head while everyone else is having a good time. On first dates it can make you seem more serious than you are. Walk in with one kind assumption about the people there, and make the first friendly move yourself.
rising.reversed:
Your own card reversed on Virgo rising can make the mask all scrutiny. You arrive already assessing, and it leaks, the raised eyebrow, the small correction, a reserve that reads as disapproval before you've said anything. People feel measured and keep their distance to match.

Because the card mirrors your rising exactly, the self-consciousness doubles as well. You can hang so far back, so sure you'll get it wrong, that you vanish from your own first impressions. It shows in rooms you leave without anyone knowing you were keen, in helpfulness that tips into fussing, and in interviews where nerves make you sound colder than you are. Mercury rules your chart and loves a detail. Pick one detail about the other person to be curious about, and ask them about it.

sun.upright:
Libra Suns find themselves through other people. Cardinal air, ruled by Venus, you work out who you are in company, by weighing things with the people you're close to and keeping the room fair and pleasant. The Hermit goes off alone and doesn't consult anybody. Virgo is Libra's next-door neighbour, and neighbouring signs share very little. On top of that, earth and air are opposed elements, so this card is pulling your Sun somewhere it doesn't naturally go.

What it's asking for is an opinion that's yours before it's anyone else's. You can see every side of a question, better than most people, and that's a real gift. The cost is that your own view sometimes goes missing while you're busy being fair to everybody else's. The Hermit wants you to sit with a choice on your own and find out what you think when there's nobody to balance against. Justice is Libra's Major, and she doesn't poll the room before she brings the sword down, so this is closer to your nature than it feels. It'll probably be uncomfortable. Libra Suns can feel slightly unreal without someone to bounce off, and that's exactly the part worth looking at.

It shows in a decision you keep taking to friends, a move, a job, whether to stay with someone. It shows at work, in ideas you've softened to keep people happy. Make the next decision on your own, write it down, and only then tell someone.
sun.reversed:
Without the Hermit's quiet, a Libra Sun can disappear into other people. With nobody to weigh yourself against you feel slightly unreal, so you defer, agree, and shape yourself to whoever's in front of you until your own preferences go silent. The solitude that would show you what you think feels like being cut adrift, so you avoid it and keep asking around.

There's a cooler version too, where you step back into a very fair-minded distance and judge from the side, refusing to commit either way. Air and earth grind here, lots of opinions and nothing to stand on. It shows in decisions put off for months, in resentment toward the people whose approval you chased, and in tiredness from pleasing. Spend an evening entirely on your own, no messages, and write down three things you want.

moon.upright:
A Libra Moon feels settled when things are nice between people. Calm voices, a pleasant room, someone to share the evening with, nobody cross. Venus rules Libra, and when there's tension in the house you feel it in your stomach. Being on your own can unsettle you too, which is where the Hermit comes in. Virgo sits one sign from Libra, neighbours with not much in common, and earth against air adds a real friction, the plain fact of how you feel against the pleasant mood you'd like to keep.

The card is asking your feelings to have some time alone, without a companion to reflect them back. At first that can feel lonely. Stay with it and a different steadiness arrives, one that doesn't depend on the person across from you being in a good mood. Libra Moons are very good at smoothing things over, often so good that they lose track of what they felt in the first place. A quiet evening is where you find it again. You might be surprised how much of your mood lately has been borrowed from someone else's.

It shows in a friendship or relationship that's a bit lopsided, which you've stayed in partly because being alone felt worse. It shows in sleep, which gets worse when someone's upset with you, and at home, in a house where there's never a room to yourself. Take one evening completely alone, let it be a bit uncomfortable, and notice what you feel when there's nobody to keep happy.
moon.reversed:
The Hermit upside down can leave a Libra Moon unable to be alone without coming apart a little. You keep the company going past the point it helps, agree to keep the peace, and lose the thread of your own feelings while you look after everyone else's. The quiet that would steady you gets avoided, so any calm you have is borrowed.

The cooler failure is going distant and even-handed to dodge an honest feeling, weighing everyone's side and never taking your own. It shows in conflict you swallow until it comes out sideways, in poor sleep when someone's annoyed with you, and in a niceness that's started to cost you. Venus rules Libra and wants everyone content. Sit with one unresolved feeling on your own, without smoothing it, and let it tell you what you actually want.

rising.upright:
Libra rising opens with charm. Venus rules your chart, so people meeting you tend to see someone graceful and easy to talk to, quick to pick up on what the other person wants and offer it. The Hermit over that door is a more self-contained figure who isn't angling to be liked at all. Virgo is the next sign along from Libra and the two share little, and air and earth pull against each other, the pleasant surface set against the plain fact, so the card cools your charm into something steadier.

You might notice you're holding a bit of yourself back at first meetings, mirroring people less and letting your own opinion sit in the room. For Libra rising that can feel almost rude. People usually take it the other way. They still find you easy to meet, and they also sense a settled person under the good manners, someone who isn't just reflecting them back. Justice, Libra's own Major, looks straight out of the card with a level gaze, and that's roughly the effect the Hermit is having on your first impression.

It shows at work, in meetings where you'd normally agree quickly and adjust later. It shows on first dates, where a real opinion early on tells you a lot about whether the other person can cope with one. With new friends it can mean letting them hear a view before you've checked it's the popular one. Meet one new person without adjusting yourself to fit them, and say what you actually think about something small.
rising.reversed:
Upside down on Libra rising, the Hermit gets refused and the mask turns into pure accommodation. You mirror so well that new people never meet you, only a pleasant surface tuned to whatever they seem to want, and afterwards you feel unseen and can't say why.

The other way it goes is a polite, cool distance, the diplomat gone aloof, sizing everyone up from behind good manners. It shows in first impressions that charm and don't stick, in relationships that start off unbalanced because you led with pleasing, and in the tiredness that comes from being agreeable all day. Venus rules your chart and is lovely when it's sincere. Meet one person as plainly as you can, opinion and all, and don't apologise for it afterwards.

sun.upright:
Scorpio Suns don't trust anything they haven't looked at from underneath. Fixed water, ruled by Mars and in modern astrology Pluto, you build yourself around depth, and you'd sooner know the hard truth than be soothed by a nice story. The Hermit is doing the same thing on his mountain, and doing it alone, which you'll also understand. Virgo makes a sextile to Scorpio, two signs apart, an easy angle, and earth and water help each other along. So the card isn't asking you to change much. It's giving your intensity some patience.

Where it helps is in what you do with everything you dig up. Scorpio has a talent for going all the way in, a person, a question, a grudge, and sometimes what you find just sits in you, heavy. The Hermit sorts. He keeps the true grain and lets the rest go, and that's a Virgo gift your Sun can borrow. Death is Scorpio's Major, a card about endings that clear the ground, and between the two there's a strong pull toward cutting away whatever isn't essential, in your work and in who you let close. The sextile is only an opening, though. You have to use it, and Scorpio Suns can prefer brooding to sorting.

It shows at work, especially anywhere that rewards research, privacy or expertise, where you're probably quietly becoming the one who knows most. It shows in shared money, handled carefully and without fuss. Take the problem you've been obsessing over and leave it alone for a week, then come back and write down what's actually true about it.
sun.reversed:
Reversed, the Hermit can send a Scorpio Sun too deep and keep it there. The retreat becomes a bunker where you brood and control and go over old wounds, and the card's careful eye turns into suspicion, reading a threat into everything. Something that should have sharpened you starts feeding on you instead.

Water and earth left still get heavy. Secrets start to isolate you, a grudge gets kept like something precious, and the intensity turns on your own sense of worth. It shows in shared money or intimacy where you hold back and watch, in sleep disturbed by what you won't say, and in people frozen out over a slight they never knew they'd given. Mars rules Scorpio and doesn't forget easily. Tell one person the thing you've been sitting on, even a small part of it.

moon.upright:
A Scorpio Moon feels everything at full depth and shows almost none of it. You need to trust someone completely before they see anything, and trust takes you years. The Hermit understands that better than most cards. Virgo makes a friendly sextile to Scorpio, and the two elements are old allies, earth holding water so it doesn't flood. What the card gives your feelings is somewhere private to have them all the way through, where nobody can use what they see against you.

That matters to you more than you'd tell anyone. A Scorpio Moon would sooner feel nothing in front of the wrong person than be caught unguarded, which means a lot gets carried around unfelt. Time alone is where it finally gets dealt with. You might be noticing how much a quiet stretch helps, and how much you resent being pulled out of it before you're done. Mars is Scorpio's traditional ruler, and a Mars Moon stays half ready for a fight. On your own, with nothing to defend, that readiness can stand down for a while, and the jaw unclenches.

It shows in intimacy, where you need to control the pace of letting someone in. It shows in sleep, which gets restless when there's something you've swallowed. With family it can be a loyalty that's absolute and a hurt that lasts just as long. Give yourself a quiet evening to feel one buried thing properly, and then trust one person with a small piece of it.
moon.reversed:
Upturned, the Hermit lets a Scorpio Moon lock the room and lose the key. The solitude that should help you feel becomes a place to store hurt and plan, and the careful eye hardens into suspicion, scanning everyone for the betrayal you've braced for.

Still water and heavy earth breed obsession here. A wound gets worked over until it's worse, and the intensity turns inward and eats at you. It shows in intimacy withheld as a way of keeping control, in sleep wrecked by what you rehearse in the dark, and in people cut off completely at the first sign of risk. Mars rules Scorpio and is always on guard. Say one true thing about how you've been to one person you trust, and don't take it back the next day.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising gives very little away at first. You watch, you listen, you decide, and people often feel they've been read before they've said a word. Mars rules your chart, with Pluto as the modern co-ruler, and there's an intensity in how you come into a room that strangers pick up even when you're quiet. The Hermit sits easily over that. Virgo is two signs from Scorpio, a sextile, and earth and water go well together, so the card's watchfulness and yours line up.

It deepens a reserve you already carry and adds some patience to it. People may sense they're with someone who sees clearly and can't be fooled, and who doesn't spend that on just anybody. For Scorpio rising that's a comfortable place to be. The risk is that people can't tell your guard from your judgement, so they assume you've judged them. Death is Scorpio's own Major, and there's something of its stillness in how you're coming across, which some people find magnetic and others find unnerving. You'll probably get both.

It shows in first meetings, where your guardedness can read as cold until you decide someone's safe, and at work, where you'll be trusted with confidential things quickly. On dates you'll come across as serious and a bit mysterious, which suits the right person. Offer one small, open thing about yourself early on, a bit of humour or a real opinion, and let the other person earn the rest.
rising.reversed:
Scorpio rising can shut the front completely when the Hermit comes up reversed. You give nothing away and watch for threat, and the intensity that could draw people in warns them off. The card's reserve doubles yours and leaves no way in.

Or the watching turns into suspicion. You read motives into everyone and test people before they've done anything, and it shows. First impressions come across as cold or unnervingly closed, relationships start with you already braced for betrayal, and your privacy gets so total it isolates you. At work, people can find you hard to approach even when they respect you. Mars rules your chart and it's quick to defend. Let one guard down on purpose with someone new, and give them a chance to prove themselves before you've decided they won't.

sun.upright:
Sagittarius Suns grow by going further. Mutable fire, ruled by Jupiter, you work out who you are by travelling, studying, arguing about big ideas, taking on a larger version of your life every few years. The Hermit has gone a long way too, all the way up a mountain, and then he's stopped. Virgo squares Sagittarius from three signs away, and both are mutable, so you're equally restless, just in opposite directions. You head out toward the whole view. The card heads in toward the one detail. Fire and earth have no natural feeling for each other either way, so this needs working at.

What it's asking of your Sun is the bit of any big plan you'd rather skip. You can see the whole shape of a thing in a flash, and then the slow middle bores you, and the middle is exactly where the Hermit sits you down. That can feel like a waste of your gifts. It isn't. Jupiter makes things bigger, and without some Virgo care the big things never quite get built. Temperance is Sagittarius's Major, a card about patience and getting the measure right, and that patience is in you. It's just rarely the first thing you reach for. A square is a friction that makes you act, so expect to be pushed into choosing one thing and staying with it.

It shows at work, where you'd sooner pitch the vision than do the follow-through it needs. It shows in study, in the course you started with real enthusiasm and dropped at the dull module. Take the plan you're most excited about and give three unhurried evenings to its most boring part.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, the Hermit can leave a Sagittarius Sun running from every detail it finds dull. You promise big, start ten things, and leave the careful finish to someone else or to nobody, and call the restlessness freedom. Jupiter rules Sagittarius and likes more of everything, including more beginnings.

The other version is a hardened certainty. You've found your big truth and you're holding it so tightly that the card's Virgo precision turns into moralising at the people around you. It shows in projects dropped at the unexciting stage, in a name for being all promise and thin delivery, and in dinner-table arguments you're sure you won and nobody else enjoyed. Pick the one thing you keep quitting and finish it quietly before you let yourself chase anything new.

moon.upright:
A Sagittarius Moon feels safest with the door open. You need room, a plan to look forward to, a joke in reserve, and the sense that if things get heavy you can always go somewhere. When a feeling hurts, you're quick to turn it into a lesson and move on. The Hermit asks for the opposite, a stretch of staying still with the feeling before you make anything of it. Virgo squares Sagittarius, two mutable signs pulling opposite ways, and fire and earth aren't naturally close, so this is a genuine stretch for your tides.

What the card holds out is the feeling you keep outrunning. You've probably noticed the reflex, the moment something gets uncomfortable and you're already looking at flights, or planning the weekend, or making everyone laugh. Jupiter rules Sagittarius and wants things to mean something, which is lovely, and it also means you can jump straight to the meaning and skip the feeling. Some things need sitting with for a while, slowly and without a moral, before they turn into anything wise. I've seen Sagittarius Moons find this very hard for about a week and then, to their surprise, restful.

It shows in sleep, which frays when you've got too many plans and no quiet. It shows in friendships where you're warm and fun and hard to reach once things get serious. With a partner it can be the conversation you keep turning into a joke. Stay in one evening with nothing planned for the next day, and let whatever comes up take as long as it takes.
moon.reversed:
The reversed Hermit can make a Sagittarius Moon bolt. The minute a feeling turns heavy you book the trip, make the plan, crack the joke, anything to keep moving, and the stillness on offer feels like a trap. So nothing gets felt all the way down, and restlessness ends up running things.

The rarer version is a flat, gloomy certainty. The usually buoyant mood collapses into this is just how it is, and the card's fussy Virgo streak picks holes in every hope you've got. It shows in plans made mainly to avoid an evening alone, in sleep broken by a mind that won't settle, and in people who find you cheerful and oddly out of reach at the same time. Cancel one escape you've lined up and spend the evening with whatever you were running from.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising comes in friendly and a bit loud. Jupiter rules your chart, and strangers usually meet someone open, funny and direct, quick with an opinion and quicker with a laugh, heading straight for the most interesting person in the room. The Hermit is about as far from that entrance as a card can get. Virgo squares Sagittarius, the same restless mode aimed the other way, toward watching and weighing before committing. Fire and earth have no natural bond, so the card and your Ascendant need a proper introduction.

What it does is slow the front end down. You might find yourself hanging back at first meetings, taking a reading before you say the blunt thing you'd normally say on sight. For Sagittarius rising that can feel like holding your breath. People around you tend to like it. Your honesty lands better when it comes after you've clearly listened, and people who might have found you a lot at first find you easy. None of the warmth has gone. You're choosing where to spend it, and Jupiter, which usually wants to hand it to everyone at once, might find that strange.

It shows in interviews, where one well-judged remark beats a string of jokes. It shows when meeting a partner's family, and in travel, where you might watch a new place for a day before throwing yourself into it. At the next gathering, let the other person do most of the talking for the first ten minutes, and notice what you'd otherwise have missed.
rising.reversed:
Sagittarius rising can steamroll the Hermit when it's reversed. You come in louder and blunter when unsure, fill the room with stories and opinions, and people leave feeling talked at. A little reserve at the door would have had you read them first.

The other way it tips is a cool, preachy distance, the open front gone certain and a bit superior, with the Virgo eye finding fault with everyone in reach. It shows in first meetings that overwhelm, in new rooms you either take over or write off, and in a bluntness that lands as tactless with people who don't know you yet. Jupiter rules your chart and makes everything bigger, first impressions included. Go in quiet once, ask one real question, and let the answer change what you were going to say.

sun.upright:
Capricorn Suns are built for the long climb. Cardinal earth, ruled by Saturn, you work out who you are through what you achieve, slowly, over years, and you don't need anyone cheering to keep going. The Hermit is an old man at the top of a mountain, and it's not hard to see why he suits you. Virgo is earth too, four signs from Capricorn in a trine, the easiest angle there is, so the card speaks your language straight away and makes the traits you already have stronger.

The good side is quiet expertise. You're likely building something that'll take a long time and speak for itself when it's done, and the Hermit gives you a sharper eye for which parts of the climb actually matter. Capricorn Suns can waste years on the parts that don't, the status, the extra hours spent being seen to work. The card's asking you to be picky. The other side is that two earth signs can turn solitude into a way of life. The Devil is Capricorn's Major, a card about the chains people put on themselves, and for a Capricorn Sun those are usually made of duty. With the Hermit on top it can look like carrying everything alone because asking would be weakness, and letting nobody close until the job's done.

At work it's a strong card for mastery, for being the person whose judgement is trusted because it's been earned. At home it asks who's waiting for you at the end of all this. Book a regular evening with someone you love, and treat it as seriously as a meeting.
sun.reversed:
The Hermit overturned on a Capricorn Sun can make the climb a prison. The discipline the card admires turns into a grind with no joy in it, and time alone stops restoring you and becomes proof that you can carry everything yourself. So you do, until it flattens you. With two earth signs stacked, nothing light comes in to break it up.

It sets in quietly. Ambition slides into control, your worth gets measured only by what you produce, and warmth waits until the work's finished. It shows in a body pushed well past tired, in relationships kept at the efficient distance of a colleague, and in a success that feels oddly empty when you get there. Saturn rules Capricorn and respects limits. Put down one duty on purpose, leave it undone, and see who actually minds.

moon.upright:
A Capricorn Moon feels safest when it's in charge of something. You keep your feelings private, you get on with it, and a finished job comforts you more reliably than a hug does. Saturn rules Capricorn, and a Saturn Moon often learned early that someone had to be the grown-up. The Hermit sits kindly on that. Virgo trines Capricorn, earth to earth, four signs apart, and both settle through quiet, useful order, so the urge to sort a feeling out privately before anyone sees it comes doubled.

That can steady you well. A clear week, a handled list, a morning with the house quiet, and you feel the ground under you again. What the doubled earth can also do is let you manage a feeling so efficiently that you never actually have it. Something sad happens and within an hour you've made a plan, rung the right people, cleared the calendar, and you feel nothing much, which you take as coping. Weeks later it turns up in your shoulders. Capricorn Moons are often the last to know they're upset, and the first to be told they're doing so well.

In the body it shows as tension in the neck, back or knees, and in sleep that goes when duty's heavy. It shows with a parent you've always felt responsible for, and in help you won't ask for because needing it feels like failing. Let one person carry something for you, even something small, and don't rush to pay them back.
moon.reversed:
A Capricorn Moon with the Hermit reversed tends to lock the feelings away and work instead. Grief or fear gets met with a longer to-do list, you tell yourself you'll deal with it once things calm down, and the retreat becomes a place to be productively numb. With earth doubled, nothing soft gets in to interrupt it.

The cost is a slow, dry loneliness you'd never call by that name. It shows in a body carrying tension it never lets go, in sleep ruined by tomorrow's obligations, and in people kept at arm's length because leaning on them feels unsafe. Saturn rules Capricorn and it's very good at enduring. Leave one small task undone and sit with whatever comes up in the gap, and tell someone you're struggling before you've got it all sorted.

rising.upright:
People take Capricorn rising seriously from the first handshake. Saturn rules your chart, and you come across as composed and capable, a little reserved, often older than you are. Put the Hermit over that and the impression gets stronger still. Virgo is earth like your Ascendant and trines Capricorn, four signs apart, so the card doubles what strangers already see, someone measured, private and good at things, who isn't performing for anyone.

That opens doors. Strangers tend to hand you responsibility early, and you rarely give a false impression, because you don't fuss to be liked. The Devil is Capricorn's own Major, and people with this rising often carry a hint of its gravity, the sense of someone who knows how the world really works. With the Hermit on top it reads as wisdom. The catch with doubled earth is that composed can look cold and reserved can look unavailable, and your warmth arrives so slowly that some people give up before it gets there. You might not even notice them going.

It shows in career, in interviews and first meetings where you'll be taken at your word. It shows in new friendships, which can take a year to get past polite. On first dates you'll seem serious and reliable, which works best with someone who wants exactly that. At the next work event, let someone see you laugh at yourself within the first few minutes.
rising.reversed:
The Capricorn mask can set hard with this card upside down. The competence that usually reassures reads as a cold front, all business, and people meet a wall of duty where they wanted a person. You default to control at the door and call it being professional.

Doubled earth keeps the guard up long past the point it helps. You're slow to warm, and slow to let anyone revise a stiff first impression. It shows in new situations handled like transactions, in a seriousness that reads as disapproval, and in colleagues who respect you and never feel they can come close. Saturn rules your chart, and when you're nervous it makes you rigid. Let one bit of humour out early in the next meeting, before you've decided whether it's safe.

sun.upright:
Aquarius Suns live a little ahead of everyone. Fixed air, ruled by Saturn in the old system and Uranus in the modern one, you build yourself around ideas, principles and the people you think with, and you're often right about where things are heading before anyone else. The Hermit comes at your Sun from an awkward angle. Virgo is five signs from Aquarius, a quincunx, which means no shared element, no shared mode, and a lot of small adjustments. Air and earth are opposed on top of that, so the friction is between the theory and whether it holds up in practice.

What the card wants is for you to take one idea off the whiteboard and test it in your own life, alone, where nobody's watching and nobody needs convincing. Aquarius tends to think in systems and for the many. The Hermit thinks in the one real case, the specific person, the actual Tuesday. That can feel small to you, and a bit like being pulled away from your people. It's also where your ideas get their proof. The Star is Aquarius's Major, a card of hope for the future, and the Hermit's lamp has a star inside it, which I've always liked. He's carrying some of your card's hope with him, only he's using it to see the next step of the path.

At work it shows in the follow-through your vision needs, the fiddly, unglamorous part that turns a good idea into something people can use. In your ideals it means living one principle out quietly before you argue it in a group. Take the cause you talk about most and do one small, practical thing for it where nobody will know.
sun.reversed:
An Aquarius Sun with the Hermit reversed can retreat into the head and call it principle. You hold the theory at a cool distance, argue the ideal, and never bring it down into the messy specifics where it'd cost you something, so the vision stays talk. The detachment looks like objectivity and is often a way of keeping your hands clean.

Or fixed air digs in, and the Virgo side of the card gets recruited to prove that everybody else is behind the times. It shows in causes argued and never lived, in a coldness that gets called being rational, and in friends kept at the range of an audience. Saturn rules Aquarius in the old system, and it asks for real work. Pick one conviction you hold and act on it in a small way that nobody will praise you for.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon keeps a little distance even from its own feelings. You understand them, explain them, file them under a theory, and stay a step back from the mess. You need freedom and a sense of belonging to something bigger, on your own terms and from a comfortable remove. The Hermit meets that from five signs away, a quincunx with no common ground, and its earthy Virgo runs straight into your airy Moon in the old argument between the idea of a feeling and the plain fact of it in the body.

What the card holds out is the feeling itself, under the explanation. You're quick to work out why you feel something and slow to just feel it. I've seen a lot of Aquarius Moons who could describe their emotional state beautifully and still seemed untouched by it, and it's lonely in there, even if it's safe. The Hermit's quiet is a place where a feeling can be physical for once, a tightness in the chest, a heaviness, tears that come without a reason attached. Saturn is Aquarius's traditional ruler, and it tends to hold things at arm's length until they're understood. Some things never quite get understood and still need feeling.

It shows in sleep, when your mind keeps running after your body's given up. It shows in friendships, which tend to be wide and friendly and not very deep. With a partner it can be the moment they ask how you feel and you tell them what you think. Sit on your own with one feeling and refuse to analyse it for twenty minutes, and notice where in the body it sits.
moon.reversed:
Everything goes into the head when the Hermit's upside down for an Aquarius Moon. Every feeling becomes a concept, discussed as if it belonged to someone else, and the quiet that could help becomes one more place to think. The detachment keeps the ache away and keeps warmth out along with it.

Fixed air holds on hard, so it sets. There's a coolness you defend as being above the drama, and the Virgo eye takes apart your own reactions until nothing's allowed to simply hurt. It shows in a loneliness you've explained to yourself, in sleep broken by a busy mind, and in people who find you friendly and never quite get let in. Put the analysis down for one evening, do something with your body, and let a feeling stay wordless until it's done.

rising.upright:
Aquarius rising is friendly with everyone and close to no one at first sight. Saturn and Uranus share your chart's rulership, depending on which system you use, and strangers tend to meet someone interested and a bit unusual, treating a new room as something fascinating to observe from slightly outside. The Hermit is a watcher too, an earthier one. Virgo is five signs from Aquarius, a quincunx, with no element or mode in common, and air and earth pull apart as well. Your rising watches the whole system, and the card watches the one concrete thing in front of it.

Handled well, this brings your overview down to the particular person you're talking to. You might notice at first meetings that the room matters less to you than one person in it, what they do, what they're worried about, why they said that. People feel the difference straight away. Aquarius rising can leave strangers feeling they've been studied kindly and not quite met, and with the Hermit over you they're likelier to feel you saw them. The Star, Aquarius's own Major, is a card that gives freely to everyone, and this card asks you to give it to one person at a time.

It shows at networking events, where one real conversation will do you more good than a dozen pleasant ones. It shows in new friendships, which can go deeper faster than you're used to. Get properly curious about one person at the next thing you go to, and ask a second question about their answer.
rising.reversed:
Aquarius rising goes remote when this card's reversed. The friendliness thins into a cool, general politeness that connects with nobody, and people feel they're being studied from behind glass. You call it being open-minded, and it's closer to not wanting to be touched.

The card's earthbound reserve keeps snagging on your airy distance, so the awkwardness doubles and you can come across as aloof or deliberately odd. It leaks into first meetings that intrigue and never warm, into rooms you analyse and don't enter, and into a coolness that leaves people unsure you liked them. Uranus, your modern ruler, likes to stand apart. Get close to one actual person at the next gathering, and stay long enough to find out something you didn't expect.

sun.upright:
Pisces Suns take the shape of whatever they're in. Mutable water, ruled by Jupiter and in modern astrology Neptune, you build yourself through imagination and feeling, and you're often at your best where edges blur, music, art, caring for people, anything you can lose yourself in. The Hermit's sign, Virgo, sits right across the zodiac from Pisces. It's your opposite, the other end of the same axis, and opposite signs tend to hold exactly what the other goes without. Earth and water are on good terms as well, so this is a kind pull toward the practical.

What the card lends your Sun is edges. You can lose a whole day, a project, sometimes a sense of who you are, to a mood or to someone else's needs, and the Hermit offers a way to sort the one true thing out of the lovely fog around it. That might sound like the opposite of what Pisces is for. It's closer to what makes your gifts usable. The Moon is Pisces's Major, a card of dreams and half-light, and the Hermit walks through much the same dark carrying a lamp. I've seen Pisces Suns pick up a bit of that light in their thirties and turn a vague gift into a real one.

At work your imagination is real, and it needs a plain structure before anyone else can use it, a deadline, a spreadsheet, a finished draft. Money and the body both drift for a Pisces Sun, and both come good under a little quiet order. Take the dream you care about most and give it one concrete shape, with a date on it.
sun.reversed:
Drifting is the usual form this takes for a Pisces Sun with the Hermit reversed. Without the card's edges you merge into whatever's around you, plans go vague, days run together, and you call it going with the flow when it's closer to dodging the plain, hard task in front of you. The escape can be a mood, a screen, a drink, or rescuing someone who didn't ask.

The other version is self-blame with no shape to it, the borrowed Virgo eye finding you wanting on every count at once. It shows in work left vague until it falls over, in money and health quietly let slide, and in dissolving into other people until you can't find yourself. Jupiter rules Pisces and doesn't love limits. Choose one real thing, give it a firm edge, a time and a finish, and keep to it.

moon.upright:
A Pisces Moon feels everything, including a lot that isn't its own. You soak up the mood of a room, the sadness of a stranger on the train, the tension between two friends at dinner, and carry it home as if it were yours. You need retreat and softness and somewhere to let it all out. The Hermit meets you from directly across the zodiac. Virgo is the sign opposite Pisces, the other end of one axis, and earth and water work kindly together, the earth giving water banks to run between.

What the card gives your tides is a way to tell your weather from other people's. That matters more for you than for almost anyone, because a Pisces Moon can carry a sadness for days before realising it was never yours. Time truly alone, with the door shut and nobody's feelings to absorb, is how that gets sorted. The Moon is Pisces's own Major, a card of dreams and things half-seen, and the Hermit's lamp is good company in that sort of light. Jupiter rules Pisces, and a Jupiter Moon is generous with its sympathy. The Hermit is asking you to keep some of it for yourself.

It shows after crowds, in how porous and worn you feel. It shows in sleep, which soaks up the day's tension and hands it back as dreams. In love it can be merging so fully that you lose track of what you wanted. Take an evening completely alone and go through what you're feeling one thing at a time, asking of each whether it's actually yours.
moon.reversed:
A Pisces Moon can go under with this card reversed. You take on so much of everyone else's feeling that your own goes missing, and time alone turns into a place to drift further. Escape starts to look like peace, and the boundaries thin to nothing.

The other face is a vague, swampy self-criticism, an ache with no edges, the Virgo eye blaming you for a heaviness you mostly picked up from other people. It shows in sleep that never quite rests, in merging so completely you lose track of what you want, and in a low mood you can't trace to anything. Neptune, the modern ruler of Pisces, loves to dissolve things. Come back to something solid, cold water on your hands, feet on the floor, and pick out one feeling that's definitely yours.

rising.upright:
Pisces rising meets the world softly. Jupiter rules your chart, with Neptune in the modern scheme, and strangers usually meet someone gentle, adaptable and a bit dreamy, whose mood shifts to match the room. The Hermit lays a clearer, more precise figure over that. Virgo faces Pisces across the zodiac, the opposite point on one axis, and opposites tend to supply what the other lacks. Earth and water get on, so this gives your fluid first impression some shape without spoiling it.

You might notice you're holding a small, clear edge at first meetings, still warm and easy, and also recognisably you. Pisces rising can mirror people so readily that afterwards you're not sure which reactions were yours, and the other person isn't sure who they met. With the Hermit over you they're more likely to come away with a definite impression, someone kind who also knows their own mind. That tends to make people trust you faster. Kindness with nothing firm behind it can leave people slightly uneasy, even when they can't say why.

It shows in interviews, where a bit of definiteness helps. It shows on first dates, where you might find yourself saying what you actually want instead of drifting toward what they do. At work it can be the meeting where you state a view and hold it. Next time you meet someone new, say one plain thing about what you like, and don't take it back when they disagree.
rising.reversed:
Pisces rising blurs completely when the card's reversed. You mirror whoever's in front of you so thoroughly that new people never meet a definite person, just a soft reflection of themselves, and afterwards you feel drained and faintly unreal.

Or it goes foggy and evasive, the gentle front slipping out of contact while the Virgo eye quietly faults you for it. It shows in first impressions that charm and never land, in relationships you enter by dissolving into the other person, and in a habit of vanishing when someone asks for something definite. At work it can look like agreeing in the meeting and quietly doing something else. Neptune, your modern ruler, blurs edges on its own. Say one plain thing that's true for you in the next conversation, and stay with it.

1.upright:
Your body, your face, your manner and the way you start things all belong to the first house. It's an angular house, one of the four corners of the chart, so what happens here gets seen. Its natural sign is Aries and its natural ruler Mars, and it's built for going first.
